name: Biomech (CR +0)
body:
What may originally come from an artificial skeleton can sometimes, through a complex understanding of biology and mechanics, be made into a sophisticated cyborg creature that is of an altogether new type of entity. Dubbed “biomechs” by many, these creatures are artificial wonders of science that transcend the normal limits of engineering.

Biomech is a template that can be applied to any construct (referred to hereafter as the base creature). A biomech uses all the base creature’s statistics and special abilities except as noted here.

Challenge Rating: Same as base creature (+0)

Type: The base creature’s type changes to aberration. However, Hit Dice, BAB, skills, and saving throws are not recalculated for the creature. The creature does lose any bonus hit points it would gain from being a sufficiently large construct.

Ability Score Modifiers: The creature gains a Constitution score of 10, which improves by +2 for every size the creature is above Small (so a Large biomech would have a Constitution score of 14). Even though it is now an aberration, a biomech that did not have an Intelligence score does not gain an Intelligence score when it gains this template. If a creature had an Intelligence score and skill list by a subtype (such as the robot subtype), it retains that Intelligence score and skill list. The creature loses any bonus hit points it would gain from being a construct or mech.

Special Qualities: Biomechs possess the following special qualities

Constructed Defenses (Ex)

Biomechs retain any construct immunities they initially possessed, but now heal naturally and can be affected by healing, positive energy, and negative energy as if they were living creatures.

Origin-Bound (Ex)

The life source of a biomech is intrinsically tied to the process originally used to construct it. If the creature possessed any subtypes or labels such as golem, mech*, or robot when it was a construct, it is still affected by abilities as if it were that type of construct in addition to the aberration type. The biomech does not need to eat, sleep, or breathe.
